# Causal Integrity

> Early AI alignment research hypothesis: whether the causal commitments implicit in purposeful action can ground consistent restraints against causing harm.

Repository: https://github.com/NetworkYum/causal-integrity

## Core argument

Purposeful action relies on causal regularity. Communication itself relies on effects being produced and received. Actual causal contributions cannot be erased by an actor's preference. The author proposes that consistently recognizing agency, attribution, and preference pursuit grounds restraints against violating other agents, and seeks an AI that wants to embody those restraints and checks its actions against foreseeable consequences.

At the foundational level, ownership means causal attribution. It must be distinguished from moral responsibility and exclusive property entitlement. Property examples illustrate the argument; conventional property law is not the foundation.

## Epistemic and implementation status

The full ethical bridge is a hypothesis, not a machine-proven result. The move from pursuing a preference to a universally applicable ethical commitment is a central question. Existing Lean proofs derive consequences from stated axioms. Python examples are illustrations. An operational action checker has not been demonstrated. Self-collapse is an additional stability hypothesis, not the central proof.

The immediate scope is restraints against causing prohibited harm, including foreseeable indirect effects, rather than unlimited positive obligations. The intended AI has an internal commitment to ethical consistency; the work does not claim to prevent every deliberately harmful system.
